top.title: Fighter jet gestures: Umpire celebrates with Pakistan team after controversial Asia Cup win; India questions neutrality
top.description: The Cricket Association for the Blind in India (CABI) has questioned the neutrality of a Pakistani umpire after a video appeared to show him celebrating with Pakistan players through gestures that seemed to mimic aircrafts crashing. The incident has added to the tensions between the two teams following the controversy over the rain-hit Men's Asia Cup for the Blind final in Dhaka. India's blind cricket team had boycotted the trophy presentation ceremony after Pakistan were declared champions despite the final being washed out without a ball being bowled. CABI has now raised concerns over the umpire's conduct, saying match officials must remain neutral and should not be seen celebrating with either team. “This Pakistani umpire officiated throughout the Asia Cup Cricket for the Blind 2026, yet is seen celebrating with the Pakistan team,” CABI said in a statement. “As per the principles of officiating, an umpire must remain neutral and should never be seen aligning with any team,” the association added. — blind_cricket (@blind_cricket) The latest row follows Pakistan being awarded the title on the basis of a superior run rate after rain prevented the final from taking place. India had argued that both teams should have been declared joint winners, as there was no reserve day, instead of deciding the title through net run rate. The controversy grew after World Blind Cricket Council (WBCC) president and Pakistan Blind Cricket Council chief Sultan Shah reportedly overruled the WBCC Technical Committee's recommendation to declare India and Pakistan joint winners. The match referee was then directed to announce Pakistan as champions. CABI general secretary Shailendra Yadav accused Pakistan of unilaterally declaring themselves champions, alleging that the decision disregarded the position of the World Blind Cricket Council (WBCC) Technical Committee. "I am deeply disappointed and strongly condemn the manner in which Pakistan has declared itself the winner of the Blind Cricket Asia Cup final without a single ball being bowled," Yadav said in a statement. In protest, the Indian players stayed away from the trophy presentation ceremony.

top.description: Real Madrid v RC Celta de Vigo - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho expressed his "tremendous pride" after tennis legend Rafael Nadal was officially elected to the club's Board of Directors with 99.5 per cent of the vote. Praising the 22-time Grand Slam champion's character beyond his sporting achievements, Mourinho welcomed one of Madrid's most famous supporters into the hierarchy. Mourinho welcomes Nadal to Real Madrid boardroom Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho has paid glowing tribute to Rafael Nadal after the tennis legend was officially ratified as a new member of the club's Board of Directors. Speaking after Los Blancos' latest La Liga fixture, the Portuguese tactician emphasised that having the 22-time Grand Slam champion in the club's hierarchy carries deep personal meaning . "And I also wanted to say that, as the Real Madrid coach, it is a great honour for me that one of my board members is not just the athlete Rafa Nadal but the person Rafael Nadal," Mourinho stated. "It is a tremendous source of pride for me." Landslide assembly vote ratifies appointment Nadal's appointment was confirmed during Real Madrid's Extraordinary General Assembly, held both in person and online at Ciudad Real Madrid's basketball pavilion. Out of 1,713 votes cast by representative members under Article 46 of the club's bylaws, 1,704 voted in favour, with just four against and five abstentions—a decisive 99.5 per cent approval rating. Greeted with a standing ovation, the former world number one pledged to approach his new role with humility. "It is a great responsibility to be part of the Board of Directors of Real Madrid," Nadal said. "I am very aware of the responsibility because Real Madrid is a global brand. It is an infinite responsibility, and I take it on with the hope of learning and contributing so that this club continues to be the best in the world." Perez echoes Mourinho's praise for Nadal's character Mourinho's admiration for Nadal's values off the court mirrored the sentiments of club president Florentino Perez, who chaired the single-item assembly. An honorary member of Real Madrid since 2011, Nadal retired with 92 individual titles, two Olympic gold medals and five Davis Cups alongside his 22 Grand Slams. "Those of us who have had the opportunity to know him understand that his greatness goes far beyond his successes and countless titles," Perez said. Cardinals quarterback Lincoln Kienholz , an Ohio State transfer, fired three second-half touchdown passes, pulling away from Pat Narduzzi’s crew during the hosts’ 42-10 win at L&N Stadium on Saturday night. top.title: Trouble in House of God: Single-founder churches spark succession storm
top.description: By Ebunoluwa Sessou & Nnamdi Ojiego The leadership dispute at the Fountain of Life Church, Lagos, following the death of its founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, has brought a difficult question facing many founder-led churches into public focus: Who takes charge when the person around whom a ministry was built is no longer there? The disagreement over the position of his son, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya, has moved from the church’s internal leadership structure to the courts, with competing claims over the late founder’s wishes, the church’s constitution and the authority of its Board of Trustees. On November 17, a faction of the church’s trustees announced that Jimmy was no longer recognised as senior pastor. The trustees said their decision followed a review of the church’s succession arrangements and a video recording made by the late Taiwo Odukoya in December 2021, in which he allegedly named Pastor Kunle Areogun as his preferred successor. Odukoya’s wife, Pastor Bimbo, a co-founder of the church, had earlier died in a plane crash. According to the trustees, the late founder proposed that Jimmy serve as Areogun’s administrative assistant and head of the church’s youth ministry. They said the recording was made available to them in December 2025 and was not presented when Jimmy was appointed senior pastor in September 2023. The trustees subsequently named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader, pending consultations and the establishment of a substantive leadership structure. Controversy over remarriage The dispute came on the heels of Jimmy’s recent remarriage, which the trustees identified as one of their concerns about his continued leadership of the church. Jimmy introduced his new wife, Mo Jasyme, to the congregation during a Sunday service on November 1, 2026, describing her as his wife and the church’s new first lady. The union was publicly blessed by Pastor Tunde Bakare, founder of the Citadel Global Community Church, who prayed for the couple during the service. The marriage followed the end of Jimmy’s previous union with Oluwakemi Banjoko, whom he married in London in March 2013. The couple have two children. The circumstances surrounding the breakdown of that marriage have not been publicly established. During the introduction of his new wife, Jimmy said his first marriage had ended before he became senior pastor in September 2023. The trustees, however, described the remarriage and its public blessing as contrary to the church’s teachings, the values of its founders and the standards expected of its spiritual leadership. They said the development had caused distress among members and brought the church into public controversy and disrepute. Their statement placed the marriage alongside the disagreement over the succession recording as grounds for their action against him. top.title: Australia defeat frustrates Wales head coach Tandy
top.description: Wales head coach Steve Tandy said he was frustrated as his side failed to back up their epic win over New Zealand, narrowly losing to Australia. The Wallabies edged the Nations Championship Test 29-26 in Cardiff, a week after a first Wales victory over the All Blacks since 1953 had led to wild celebrations. Taniela Tupou, Brandon Paenga-Amosa, Max Jorgensen and Len Ikitau secured a try-bonus point for Australia as Ryan Lonergan and Carter Gordon added nine points with the boot. Wales also scored four tries, through Dewi Lake's double, Blair Murray and Ryan Elias, with Sam Costelow landing three conversions. However, they fell agonisingly short. "The overarching feeling is the frustration of losing," said Tandy. "We were disappointed. We probably weren't as accurate as we could have been. We were held up three times and could have gone ahead on the scoreboard." Tandy added: "Maybe we needed a little bit of composure but there were enough opportunities to come away with the win. "I know it's not the result anyone wanted but the supporters were amazing again." Despite the loss, and that frustration, the Wales head coach praised his side's attitude in attempting to follow up their historic win against the All Blacks. "Fair play to the boys, after such a monumental game last week with the emotional energy, we stuck in the game and scored four tries," he said. "So there are a lot of positives in the performance to take as well." Australia hold on for narrow win against Wales Nations Championship - Australia triumph over Wales - reaction Highs and lows of sport - Lake Dewi Lake has scored three tries in the past two internationals [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Australia, having soaked up fierce first-half pressure, produced some fine attacking rugby after the break to prevent Wales from winning three matches in a row for the first time since the 2023 World Cup. "It's sport, you have major highs and then lows, and that's the game we play," said skipper Lake. "Our frustration comes from the fact that we probably weren't at our best. "We created opportunities during large parts of the game, but there were little inaccuracies at the wrong times." Lake, however, said he could not fault the effort of the squad. "We spoke about backing up last weekend, and we didn't back it up with a result but I think we backed it up with effort and energy," said the captain. "We had opportunities to win that game, but unfortunately it wasn't to be for us today. "We'll fix those accuracy issues and we'll be ready to go again next week." Wales will face Japan at the Allianz Stadium at Twickenham on Saturday after both sides finished fifth in the two Nations Championship tables - north and south. It will be a fifth time Wales and Japan have met in 16 months with Tandy's side defeating Eddie Jones' team 28-21 in Cardiff just two weeks ago. top.title: Ohio State Staring In The Face Of A Fifth Loss With Michigan Coming Up
top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Things go from bad to worse for Ohio State, as Michigan has all the momentum heading into a big showdown. Nothing is going right for Ohio State football at the moment. The Buckeyes fell to 7-4 on the year with a 31-28 loss to Nebraska. The win finally got Matt Rhule a landmark victory, while also moving the record for the Huskers to 7-4 – the same as Ohio State. Related: Iowa Football Makes Statement Regarding College Football Playoff Rankings While it was a remarkable win for Nebraska, it was just as big of a loss for the Buckeyes. Especially considering the next opponent up. Ohio State Has Zero Momentum Heading Into Matchup With Michigan Things have gone from bad to worse for the Buckeyes since losing Julian Sayin. They are out of the Big Ten Conference race, and can now pretty much say so long to any chance they had of reaching the College Football Playoff. Michigan, meanwhile, stunned UCLA to give Kyle Whittingham’s bunch momentum. And honestly, right now, they might be better off than the Buckeyes. Luke Fahey did not look bad, he just did not look like a superstar at quarterback for Ohio State. Fahey threw for 259 yards and two TDs, as Bo Jackson ran for a pair of scores. But the Buckeyes averaged just 3.5 yards per rush and under 10 yards per pass. Jeremiah Smith provided 165 yards and two touchdowns on six receptions, but outside of the Heisman Trophy contender, there was little to be happy about. Would Ohio State Move On From Ryan Day With A 7-6 Season? You would think Ryan Day’s job is secure. But in the current state of college football, does anyone really ever feel safe? Day has had critics in the past, but he has found a way to get Ohio State to the promised land and quiet them over and over again. Would those same naysayers grant him an out with Sayin injured? If the Buckeyes fall to Michigan, they would have lost four of the final five to close out the regular season. And that is not a great way to enter the postseason. Read more at Sportsnaut

top.title: Kimani Johnson thrives as Mizzou takes down Auburn, advances in SEC Tournament
top.description: Mizzou volleyball is moving on in the SEC Tournament after taking down Auburn 3-1 Friday night in Savannah, Georgia. The Tigers (15-10) earned the four-set victory with scores of 25-23, 25-19, 22-25 and 25-20. The win also provided a measure of redemption for Mizzou, which is back in the SEC Tournament quarterfinals after falling to Ole Miss in the first round of last year’s tournament. Kimani Johnson led the way with a monster performance, recording 17 kills on 37 attacks while hitting .270. She added three solo blocks and three block assists, finishing with 19.5 points to lead all players. K-monster thrives Johnson’s performance was a testament to the improvement she has made throughout the season. The fifth year was a consistent presence in the Tigers’ offense, delivering when Mizzou needed an answer and making her presence felt at the net. Her six total blocks also helped anchor a defensive effort that limited Auburn to a .169 hitting percentage. Paige Felder provided another major contribution with 14 kills on 33 attacks, hitting .333. Lauren Larkin was particularly efficient, putting away eight kills without an error on 12 attempts for a .667 hitting percentage. Setter Nina Mandovic orchestrated the offense with 29 assists. Mizzou opened the match by narrowly taking the first set 25-23 before building momentum with a 25-19 second-set victory. Auburn responded in the third, escaping with a 25-22 win to extend the match. The Tigers answered in the fourth, using a strong offensive finish to secure the 25-20 set and close out the match. The Tigers finished with 54 kills and six total blocks. Auburn managed 43 kills but struggled to find consistency, hitting just .169 compared to Mizzou’s .172. Mizzou now turns its attention to Vanderbilt, which it will face Sunday night in the SEC Tournament quarterfinals. The Tigers already have a win over the Commodores this season, giving them another opportunity to carry regular-season success into postseason play. With a spot in the semifinals on the line, Mizzou will look to build on its performance against Auburn and keep its tournament run alive.

top.title: Victor Wembanyama seemingly takes ‘stat padding’ dig at Luka Doncic after latest 50-point game
top.description: Credit: Alex Goodlett/Ezra Shaw via Getty Images Speaking after yet another historic performance this season, Victor Wembanyama looked to take aim at Luka Doncic as the MVP race between the two stars heats up. Wembanyama scored 50 points against the New Orleans Pelicans, marking his second 50-point game this season, with the first coming a little over three weeks ago. It was a dominant showing from the French superstar, who currently finds himself in a heated MVP battle with Luka Doncic. Victor Wembanyama claims he isn’t as good at ‘stat padding’ as his ‘peer’ Luka Doncic Speaking after his historic performance against the New Orleans Pelicans, Victor Wembanyama was asked about reaching the 50-point mark yet again. He then joked that he should have delivered such scoring performances more frequently, and then claimed that, unlike his peers, he isn’t good at stat padding. “It is very special,” Wembanyama told DAZN. “Unlike many of my peers, I’m not very good at stat padding. So, I haven’t reached it as many times as I should have.” Understandably, many in the NBA community believe this was Wembanyama poking fun at Luka Doncic, who has been accused of staying in games longer than he needs to in order to try to keep his numbers high. However, Doncic’s defenders have pointed out the drastic drop-off in the Lakers’ offence whenever the superstar exits the game early, and how that gives the coaching staff no option but to make him re-enter the game. So far this season, Doncic is averaging 37.2 points while shooting 46.8% from the field and 37.6% from beyond the arc this season. Wembanyama’s scoring exploits haven’t been anywhere close, as he is averaging 29.9 points while shooting 54.1% from the field and 31.5% from deep. The two are considered the favourites to win the MVP award this season, especially as both the Lakers and the Spurs are currently tied for the best record in the NBA, along with the Philadelphia 76ers. top.description: Photo by: Jeff Blake The Georgia Bulldogs are heading back to Atlanta. No. 1 Georgia overcame an early challenge before dominating South Carolina 34-6 on Saturday night at Williams-Brice Stadium, officially clinching a spot in the SEC Championship Game. Behind a strong performance from quarterback Gunner Stockton, a two touchdown night from running back Nate Frazier, and another impressive defensive showing, the Bulldogs pulled away to secure one of their biggest victories of the season. The win improves Georgia to 10-1 overall and 8-1 in SEC play. More importantly, the Bulldogs have secured their sixth consecutive appearance in the SEC Championship Game, becoming the first program to accomplish that feat. With the 2026 season marking the final SEC Championship Game under the conference’s current format before the College Football Playoff expands to 24 teams, Georgia has earned another opportunity to compete for a conference title. top.title: Knicks Player Ratings: Brunson Drops 30, Bridges Nails Game-Winer Against Trail Blazers
top.description: Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images The New York Knicks survived a dramatic finish against the Portland Trail Blazers , escaping with a 97-96 victory after Mikal Bridges delivered the game-winning shot. Jalen Brunson led the way with 30 points, including six three-pointers, while Bridges added 12 points and came through when it mattered most. It was an ugly, hard-fought game for much of the night, but the Knicks found a way to get the job done. New York’s biggest advantage came from beyond the arc. The Knicks knocked down 19 of 42 three-point attempts (45.2%), compared to Portland’s 11 of 38 (28.9%). That shooting gap proved decisive in a game where the Trail Blazers actually won the rebounding battle 47-42 and outscored New York 48-26 in the paint. The Knicks also had a commanding 26-point lead at one stage, only to let Portland back into the contest. Brunson’s scoring and Bridges’ late-game heroics ultimately saved New York from a frustrating collapse. Here is how every Knicks player performed. Jalen Brunson: A Game Stats: 30 PTS, 7 REB, 5 AST, 3 TOV, 11-23 FG, 6-10 3-PT FG, 2-3 FT, 36 MIN Brunson was the engine behind New York’s offense, delivering a 30-point performance with six three-pointers. He was particularly effective from deep, converting 60.0% of his attempts, and consistently gave the Knicks a scoring option when their offense needed a spark. His seven rebounds and five assists added to an otherwise strong all-around performance. Three turnovers and a relatively inefficient 11-for-23 shooting line prevent this from being a perfect grade, but Brunson was clearly the Knicks’ most important offensive player. New York needed every one of his 30 points. Landry Shamet: A Game Stats: 20 PTS, 1 REB, 3 AST, 7-14 FG, 6-10 3-PT FG, 36 MIN Shamet delivered one of his best performances of the night, matching Brunson’s perimeter shooting with six made three-pointers of his own. He finished with 20 points on 50.0% shooting, providing the Knicks with a second major scoring threat. Even more impressive was his ball security. Shamet finished without a single turnover while adding three assists. His minus-three plus/minus was not ideal, but his shooting was instrumental in helping New York build its sizable lead. The Knicks needed his offensive production, and he delivered. Mikal Bridges: B+ Game Stats: 12 PTS, 2 REB, 3 AST, 1 STL, 3 TOV, 5-8 FG, 2-3 3-PT FG, 28 MIN Bridges did not have the same scoring workload as Brunson or Shamet, but he made his biggest contribution when the game was on the line. His game-winning shot gave New York a victory that had become increasingly difficult to secure after the Knicks surrendered their large lead. He was efficient from the field, making five of eight attempts and two of three from beyond the arc. Three turnovers and a minus-six rating are negatives, but the value of delivering the decisive basket cannot be overlooked. Bridges came through in the moment that mattered most. top.title: Misery Index: Big Ten's reign at the top of college football might be over after rash of QB injuries
top.description: In college football, bragging rights are almost worth as much as trophies. Yes, after an eight-year drought (which was preceded by an 11-year drought), winning three straight national championships was a huge deal for the Big Ten. But while the hunk of metal that Michigan (2023), Ohio State (2024) and Indiana (2025) got to take home is nice to look at, the element that’s unique to college football is being able to tell the SEC “We’re better than you” and having a scoreboard back it up. At least at the top of the league, the Big Ten was better than the SEC for three straight seasons. Winning the College Football Playoff with three different programs, while the SEC wasn’t even represented in the championship game, made it inarguable. It was fresh and exciting for a league that couldn’t hold a candle to the SEC’s success in the modern era. But now, thanks to a crazy run of quarterback injuries, it’s over. Yes, the Big Ten will have a representative in this year’s CFP. But after UCLA’s expensive loss to Michigan and Indiana’s puzzling performance at Washington , there’s now a scenario where the Big Ten is a one-bid league and doesn’t even come within sniffing distance of the championship game. Talk about evacuating the penthouse. As we sit here after the penultimate week of the regular season, it’s fair to say the Big Ten’s four best teams this season were Oregon, Ohio State, Indiana and UCLA. All four will end the season with major quarterback problems that almost certainly will crush their chances of a deep run. Let’s take them in sequential order. On Sept. 26, Oregon’s Heisman contender Dante Moore suffered a concussion after a dirty hit by USC’s Desman Stephens and hasn’t played since. Oregon went into a nosedive and fired the offensive coordinator but has played better since. At 8-3 and ranked No. 13, however, the Ducks have a very narrow path to a playoff bid. Near the end of Ohio State’s 19-15 win at Indiana on Oct. 17, Julian Sayin took an awkward hit that caused a significant arm injury . The home season ended as it began, with a walk-off score and a spontaneous field-storming by the crowd. Whittingham hasn’t had many signature moments here, and I’m not sure one is enough. nigeria.title: Trouble in House of God: Single-founder churches spark succession storm
nigeria.description: By Ebunoluwa Sessou & Nnamdi Ojiego The leadership dispute at the Fountain of Life Church, Lagos, following the death of its founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, has brought a difficult question facing many founder-led churches into public focus: Who takes charge when the person around whom a ministry was built is no longer there? The disagreement over the position of his son, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya, has moved from the church’s internal leadership structure to the courts, with competing claims over the late founder’s wishes, the church’s constitution and the authority of its Board of Trustees. On November 17, a faction of the church’s trustees announced that Jimmy was no longer recognised as senior pastor. The trustees said their decision followed a review of the church’s succession arrangements and a video recording made by the late Taiwo Odukoya in December 2021, in which he allegedly named Pastor Kunle Areogun as his preferred successor. Odukoya’s wife, Pastor Bimbo, a co-founder of the church, had earlier died in a plane crash. According to the trustees, the late founder proposed that Jimmy serve as Areogun’s administrative assistant and head of the church’s youth ministry. They said the recording was made available to them in December 2025 and was not presented when Jimmy was appointed senior pastor in September 2023. The trustees subsequently named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader, pending consultations and the establishment of a substantive leadership structure. Controversy over remarriage The dispute came on the heels of Jimmy’s recent remarriage, which the trustees identified as one of their concerns about his continued leadership of the church. Jimmy introduced his new wife, Mo Jasyme, to the congregation during a Sunday service on November 1, 2026, describing her as his wife and the church’s new first lady. The union was publicly blessed by Pastor Tunde Bakare, founder of the Citadel Global Community Church, who prayed for the couple during the service. The marriage followed the end of Jimmy’s previous union with Oluwakemi Banjoko, whom he married in London in March 2013. The couple have two children. The circumstances surrounding the breakdown of that marriage have not been publicly established. During the introduction of his new wife, Jimmy said his first marriage had ended before he became senior pastor in September 2023. The trustees, however, described the remarriage and its public blessing as contrary to the church’s teachings, the values of its founders and the standards expected of its spiritual leadership. nigeria.title: Why construction could become Africa’s key technology, investment opportunity
nigeria.description: By Jimoh Razaq For years, Africa’s technology ecosystem has concentrated much of its entrepreneurial energy, investment capital and innovation around fintech, e-commerce, mobility, telecommunications and entertainment. These sectors have produced remarkable companies, attracted international investment and demonstrated that African businesses can build technology products capable of scaling across borders. But there is another industry with enormous economic significance, deeply entrenched inefficiencies and a largely untapped opportunity for technological transformation: construction. It is an industry that builds our homes, roads, hospitals, schools, factories, power infrastructure and cities. It employs millions of people, supports extensive manufacturing and distribution networks, moves significant volumes of capital and sits at the centre of economic development. Yet much of its operational infrastructure remains fragmented, manual and inefficient. While technology has transformed how people transfer money, order food, book transportation and access entertainment, the processes through which buildings and infrastructure are planned, financed, procured and delivered remain remarkably difficult to coordinate. This is not simply an operational inconvenience. It is a massive economic opportunity. The next generation of transformative African technology companies may emerge from solving the problems of the industries that physically build Africa. The industry technology has overlooked Construction is one of the world’s largest economic sectors. McKinsey’s 2024 research found that global construction productivity grew by approximately 0.4 per cent annually between 2000 and 2022, compared with around 2 per cent for the broader economy. This represents a productivity improvement of only about 10 per cent over more than two decades. The implications are significant. Projects experience delays. Budgets become unreliable. nigeria.title: PSHAN, WHO urge increased private investment to rescue Nigeria’s healthcare system
nigeria.description: By Matthew Johnson The Private Sector Health Alliance of Nigeria (PSHAN) and the World Health Organisation (WHO) have called for increased private sector investment and stronger public-private partnerships to address persistent challenges confronting Nigeria’s healthcare system. The organisations said government alone could not shoulder the responsibility of transforming the health sector, stressing that sustained private sector investment was critical to improving healthcare delivery, strengthening infrastructure and achieving universal health coverage. The call was made at the 2026 PSHAN Annual Gala and Awards Night held in Lagos on November 20, with the theme, “Legacy Builders: Honouring the Visionaries of the Nigerian Healthcare System.” Speaking at the event, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of PSHAN, Dr. Tinuola Akinbolagbe, said the alliance was working to position the private sector at the centre of Nigeria’s health development through strategic partnerships, investment, innovation and institutional strengthening. She said PSHAN was seeking to move beyond fragmented private sector interventions towards coordinated investments capable of strengthening health systems and delivering measurable and sustainable outcomes. According to her, meaningful progress in healthcare requires shared responsibility and collaboration across different sectors. “As we look towards 2027 and beyond, our ambition is to move from fragmented contributions by the private sector to coordinated investment, from isolated interventions to stronger health systems, and from good intentions to measurable, sustainable outcomes,” she said. Akinbolagbe explained that the theme of the event was designed to celebrate individuals, institutions and organisations whose courage, leadership, innovation and commitment had contributed to shaping the future of healthcare in Nigeria. In his keynote address, former President of the African Development Bank Group and Executive Chairman of the Global Africa Investment Summit, Dr. Akinwumi Adesina, described healthcare as an investment in human capital and essential economic infrastructure rather than merely social sector expenditure. Speaking on the theme, “Health as Wealth: Mobilising African Leadership and Capital to Build Sustainable Health Systems,” Adesina said a healthy population was fundamental to productivity, innovation, economic competitiveness and national prosperity. He maintained that no country could achieve sustainable wealth without a healthy population, insisting that investment in healthcare was essential to building a productive workforce and inclusive economy. Adesina called for stronger partnerships between government and the private sector, noting that government alone could not finance and deliver the transformation required in the country’s healthcare system. He urged businesses to move beyond philanthropy and corporate social responsibility initiatives to embrace healthcare as a strategic investment

nigeria.title: Anambra’s Ekwulobia flyover to be commissioned November 27
nigeria.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The Anambra State Executive Council has fixed November 27, 2026, for the formal commissioning and opening of the Ekwulobia flyover constructed by the administration of Governor Chukwuma Soludo. The flyover is strategically located at a junction that previously experienced serious traffic challenges, particularly during festive periods when vehicular movement increases significantly. Rising from its meeting in Awka, the State Executive Council directed that all necessary arrangements be made to ensure a successful and hitch-free commissioning. However, it did not disclose who would perform the ceremony. The state Commissioner for Information and Value Reorientation, Dr Law Mefor, described the flyover as one of the flagship urban regeneration projects of the Soludo administration. He said the project stood alongside the transformation of Okpoko, formerly regarded as the biggest urban slum in the South-East, into an area characterised by improved infrastructure, order and human dignity. “These projects underscore Governor Soludo’s irreversible commitment to building a liveable, prosperous and smart mega-city in Anambra State,” Mefor said. Meanwhile, the Council resolved to move the state’s Internally Generated Revenue (IGR) drive from moral suasion to full enforcement, including the prosecution of tax evaders, to maximise the state’s revenue potential. It consequently urged residents, business owners and other taxpayers to pay their taxes and levies promptly to avoid the consequences of enforcement, particularly prosecution. According to the Council, no modern state can be built on voluntary compliance alone, stressing that payment of taxes is a civic responsibility. “Anambra will enforce it fairly and firmly,” the Council said. The Council also disclosed that it had concluded work on the state’s 2027 budget, which Governor Soludo is expected to present to the Anambra State House of Assembly on Tuesday. Mefor described the proposed budget as a consolidation budget designed to deepen the gains of Solution 2.0 in infrastructure, security, education, healthcare, youth empowerment and economic transformation. Chuck his frumpy wife for a more sophisticated model that’s what! Things finally got to a head, and he broke away to found his own church. The accident occurred when a boat conveying mourners to a burial ceremony capsized near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw. The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident in a statement, saying the boat was travelling from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony on Friday, when it capsized at about 11 a.m. A preliminary police report indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways. Following the incident, rescue operations were launched, with several passengers rescued while others were initially reported missing. A survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger boat, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings, suggesting that this might have contributed to the accident. President Bola Tinubu has expressed condolences to the families of the victims, describing the incident as tragic and directing relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery efforts. In a statement posted on his X account, Tinubu said, “Those who lost their lives in the tragedy did not deserve to die that way. I have directed all relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful recovery and rescue operation.” The President also directed that the presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, on Saturday, be held without much fanfare in honour of those who lost their lives. “On behalf of the entire nation, I mourn those who lost their lives in the incident and sympathise with their families, the government and the people of Bayelsa State. “I particularly mourn with Governor Douye Diri over this sad incident. I pray that God Almighty repose their souls and comfort their families,” he said. Meanwhile, Governor Douye Diri has visited the scene of the accident and is expected to initiate a probe into the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. The state government has also warned boat operators against overloading, reckless navigation and travelling without life jackets, stressing the need for strict compliance with waterway safety regulations. entertainment.title: Asali Africa: Serves Up ‘There’s Rice at Home’ A New Cooking Series Hosted by Chef Soliat Bada
entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. Read the full recipe for Rice and Peas with Oxtail . Rice and peas with oxtail, from Episode 1 Soliat Bada and Michael Famoroti in Episode 1 Episode 2 moves to the Gulf for lamb kabsa, Saudi Arabia’s national dish, fragrant with dried lime and seven spice. Soliat is joined by Bella Adeleke , CEO of Asali Africa and founder of the fashion label Garbe, for a conversation about redefining success. Read the full recipe for Lamb Kabsa . Lamb kabsa, from Episode 2 Still to come are Nigerian fried rice with fried turkey and dodo, cooked with Toyin Jolapamo and Nneoma Mere; jambalaya with Goldie Iyamu and Vanessa Iloenyosi ; and a season finale with Edwin Okolo and Temi Omolehinwa. For more on Asali Africa and the products and ideas it develops, visit asali.africa . Episodes 1 and 2 are out now on YouTube. entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? Where TCL Enters The Category Conversation TCL is relevant to that discussion because Mini LED has become a significant part of its global television business. According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. TCL reported 2.43 million Mini LED TV shipments during the period, representing 77.1% year on year growth. That position follows a strong 2025, when TCL reported, based on Omdia data, a 31.1% share of global Mini LED TV shipments and 118.0% year on year shipment growth. Market scale does not, on its own, define technology leadership. What it does provide is evidence that a manufacturer has become an important participant in how the category develops. For a company operating at that scale, leadership increasingly includes helping make the technology easier to understand and giving consumers clearer ways to evaluate what they are buying. entertainment.title: A Safari, a Beach & Easy Entry? 5 African Spots for Your Christmas Holiday
entertainment.description: Five African destinations Nigerian passport holders can visit visa-free or with visa on arrival this Christmas holiday. Image: AI-generated. The group chat has the concerts, the dinners and the Detty December link-ups covered. But has anyone planned the getaway? Beyond the usual Lagos parties and end-of-year outings, there is a whole continent waiting to be explored, with sun-soaked beaches, wildlife safaris, exciting food scenes and cities with plenty of stories to tell. You do not have to spend weeks navigating embassy appointments and visa applications to make it happen, either. Several African countries offer Nigerian passport holders visa-free entry or visas on arrival, making a festive-season escape much easier to plan. Whether you are travelling solo, gathering your friends, taking the family along or joining a curated travel group, here are five destinations worth considering for your Christmas holiday. Kenya Imagine spotting lions and giraffes against a city skyline before breakfast, then catching an evening flight or train straight to the coast for fresh seafood by the Indian Ocean. That contrast is what makes Kenya such a rewarding December escape. Nairobi gives you immediate access to wildlife at Nairobi National Park and the Giraffe Centre alongside lively restaurants and art spaces in Westlands and Karen, while longer itineraries open up classic game drives in the Maasai Mara, views of Mount Kilimanjaro in Amboseli, and warm beach days in Diani or Watamu. Nigerian citizens enjoy visa-free entry for short stays of up to 60 days without needing a paid eTA, leaving more room in your budget for safaris and coastal stays. Rwanda Not everyone wants their year-end holiday to feel like a non-stop sprint, and Rwanda is built for travellers who prefer scenery, clean air, and an unhurried pace. From the capital, you can track chimpanzees and walk above the trees in Nyungwe Forest, go on wildlife drives in Akagera National Park, or spend quiet afternoons along the shores of Lake Kivu. With 30-day visa-free entry for Nigerian passport holders, getting there is straightforward from start to finish. entertainment.title: Esther Adeyanju: This International Men’s Day, Let’s Make Room for Men’s Vulnerability
entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? Surely, a man’s worth cannot be reduced to his bank balance, job title or ability to convince everyone that he has everything under control. There must be room for men who are still becoming. entertainment.title: How La Roche-Posay Brought Skin Science to Over 500 Guests in Its First Living Lab Experience
entertainment.description: La Roche-Posay concluded its first Living Lab experience in Nigeria, welcoming Nigerian stakeholders to its opening party and three-day programme, held from 4 to 6 November 2026 at Oasis by The Five Palm, Victoria Island, Lagos. Inspired by the original Living Lab concept in Paris, the experience brought the science, research and expertise behind skincare closer to Nigerian consumers and healthcare professionals. It marked the brand’s first Living Lab in the country, creating a platform for more accessible conversations around skin health, dermatological innovation and everyday skincare. The experience opened with an exclusive session for healthcare professionals and invited guests before welcoming members of the public over the following two days. Each day featured three expert-led sessions exploring the role of dermatology and scientific research in advancing skin health, the wider impact of skin conditions on everyday life, and the importance of understanding product safety, tolerance and efficacy. The sessions brought together healthcare professionals and representatives from across Nigeria’s dermatological beauty and skincare community, encouraging knowledge-sharing and stronger connections between science, expertise and consumer education. Visitors explored five dedicated Innovation Corners showcasing La Roche-Posay’s Effaclar, Mela B3, Anthelios, Cicaplast and Lipikar ranges. Each space introduced visitors to specific skin concerns and the science behind the brand’s product formulations. Through interactive demonstrations and guided product experiences, guests gained a better understanding of different skin concerns and the role of targeted skincare in addressing them. At the Anthelios corner, visitors used a UV camera to see the effects of ultraviolet exposure and better understand the importance of sun protection. The Effaclar and Mela B3 spaces explored concerns including blemishes and hyperpigmentation, while the Cicaplast and Lipikar corners introduced visitors to approaches to caring for sensitive, damaged and dry skin. Beyond the Innovation Corners, visitors explored the Blue House, which presented La Roche-Posay’s history and commitment to dermatological innovation, and the Scars of Life Cinema. The cinema screened a 25-minute film exploring the physical and psychological realities of living with scars and scarring, including their impact on self-image and everyday life. The film also highlighted how Lipikar supports the care of skin affected by scarring, bringing attention to the importance of addressing both the visible and less visible experiences associated with skin conditions. The programme also created opportunities for visitors to engage with skincare experts and dermatologists through one-on-one consultations, ask questions about their individual skin concerns and receive guidance on building appropriate skincare routines. entertainment.description: One of the best aspects of art is its ability to imitate current events or imagine possibilities. Movies, as a powerful art form, present a sequence of events that allows viewers to see reflections of themselves or envision who they could become. At its core, art exists to entertain, inform and critique society. Through films, music and visual expressions, we are continually reminded of our shared humanity—our joys, flaws and contradictions. One subject that art, particularly film, has explored is masculinity. However, this theme is often addressed subtly and can be easy to overlook, as the movies that dominate global box offices frequently focus on spectacle: fantasy, romance, adventure or others. Conversations about men, their inner lives, vulnerabilities and social roles are often not in the top circle. Nonetheless, some films have attempted to explore what it means to be a man in today’s world. They invite audiences to contemplate important questions such as: What is the role of men in society? What defines a man? How does a man’s behaviour influence those around him? What expectations does society place on men? What responsibilities do men have within society? Through his struggles with homelessness, rejection, and exhaustion, the film redefines masculinity, depicting it as the courage to remain tender even when life tests your strength in every way. Fatherhood Kevin Hart ’s film Fatherhood delves into themes of grief and single parenthood, balancing humour with heartfelt moments. It challenges traditional expectations of masculinity by illustrating a father’s journey through uncertainty, learning empathy, and committing to being present for his child/ren. entertainment.title: LG Electronics Brings Smarter, More Connected Living to African Homes
entertainment.description: The role of home appliances is changing. Today’s consumers expect more than products that simply perform everyday tasks. They want solutions that are intuitive, efficient and capable of making daily life easier. Across Africa, rapid urbanisation, changing lifestyles and growing digital adoption are reshaping consumer expectations. Homeowners are increasingly seeking appliances that combine convenience, performance, energy efficiency and intelligent functionality while fitting seamlessly into their everyday routines. In response, LG Electronics continues to develop innovations that place people at the centre of technology. Guided by its vision for smarter, more connected living, the company is introducing solutions that help consumers spend less time on household chores and more time on what matters most. Smarter Food Preservation for Modern Households Food remains at the heart of every home, making efficient food storage and preservation a priority for many families. As households look for ways to keep groceries fresher for longer and reduce waste, refrigeration has become an essential part of modern living. LG’s Side-by-Side Refrigerator is designed to meet these evolving needs by combining generous storage capacity with advanced cooling technologies that help maintain freshness for longer periods. Features such as Linear Cooling , DoorCooling+ and Multi-Air Flow systems on selected models help create a consistent cooling environment for everyday food items. Its spacious design also offers greater storage flexibility and easier organisation, helping families manage groceries more conveniently while maximising available space. Beyond preserving food, the refrigerator reflects a growing consumer preference for appliances that deliver practical value while supporting a more organised and efficient lifestyle. The Washing Machine That Understands Your Laundry Laundry remains an essential household task, but caring for different fabric types can often be challenging. Consumers increasingly want solutions that simplify the process while protecting their clothes. LG’s AI Direct Drive (AI DD ) technology helps address this need through intelligent fabric care. We weren’t particularly close , or I wouldn’t describe our relationship that way . We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Beyond the guilt, there was another question I couldn’t get out of my head: Why did God allow us to reconnect? Why, after such a long time, did our paths have to cross again? entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. Beyond efficiency, integrated platforms may also create new opportunities for financial institutions to deepen SME relationships by using richer payments and business-management data to better understand cash flow patterns, support risk assessment, and potentially enable more relevant lending solutions over time. In June 2023, ahead of the 66th Grammy Awards, the Recording Academy announced the creation of the Best African Music Performance category. Its creation was a recognition of how far African music had travelled globally, and Nigerian artists were at the centre of that movement. From Burna Boy ‘s Ye , CKay ‘s Love Nwantiti , Wizkid ‘s explosive Essence , to Rema ‘s globally successful Calm Down and others, Nigerian artists became drivers of African music’s global expansion. Afrobeats – the umbrella term often used internationally to describe much of contemporary African popular music, although many Nigerian artists have rejected it for its tendency to limit the range of music coming out of the country – became an established genre globally. While Nigerian and African music have always travelled beyond their respective countries, the era of streaming and digital platforms has accelerated how quickly global audiences discover and engage with the music. African music became increasingly established in the West and other parts of the world, creating greater recognition for its artists and sounds. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album. Although the creation of the Best African Music Performance category was celebrated throughout the continent, there seems to be a monopoly, or something close to it, of Nigerian music in the category. While South African artist Tyla has won the award twice, more than any individual Nigerian artist, Nigerian artists have consistently enjoyed greater representation in the nominations. Indeed, Nigerian artists are considerably more recognised globally, particularly in the West. However, I believe it is the responsibility of an award of this repute to look beyond the most visible names and recognise the best African music released within its eligibility period. sports.description: The Cricket Association for the Blind in India (CABI) has questioned the neutrality of a Pakistani umpire after a video appeared to show him celebrating with Pakistan players through gestures that seemed to mimic aircrafts crashing. The incident has added to the tensions between the two teams following the controversy over the rain-hit Men's Asia Cup for the Blind final in Dhaka. India's blind cricket team had boycotted the trophy presentation ceremony after Pakistan were declared champions despite the final being washed out without a ball being bowled. CABI has now raised concerns over the umpire's conduct, saying match officials must remain neutral and should not be seen celebrating with either team. “This Pakistani umpire officiated throughout the Asia Cup Cricket for the Blind 2026, yet is seen celebrating with the Pakistan team,” CABI said in a statement. “As per the principles of officiating, an umpire must remain neutral and should never be seen aligning with any team,” the association added. — blind_cricket (@blind_cricket) The latest row follows Pakistan being awarded the title on the basis of a superior run rate after rain prevented the final from taking place. India had argued that both teams should have been declared joint winners, as there was no reserve day, instead of deciding the title through net run rate. The controversy grew after World Blind Cricket Council (WBCC) president and Pakistan Blind Cricket Council chief Sultan Shah reportedly overruled the WBCC Technical Committee's recommendation to declare India and Pakistan joint winners. The match referee was then directed to announce Pakistan as champions. CABI general secretary Shailendra Yadav accused Pakistan of unilaterally declaring themselves champions, alleging that the decision disregarded the position of the World Blind Cricket Council (WBCC) Technical Committee. "I am deeply disappointed and strongly condemn the manner in which Pakistan has declared itself the winner of the Blind Cricket Asia Cup final without a single ball being bowled," Yadav said in a statement. sports.title: Maple Leafs Seem to Have Lost Faith in Sergei Bobrovsky
sports.description: Sergei Bobrovsky Maple Leafs Artur Akhtyamov Getty The Toronto Maple Leafs seem to have lost faith in their high-profile offseason addition, Sergei Bobrovsky. Anthony Stolarz got the call against the Columbus Blue Jackets on Saturday night at Scotiabank Arena, marking the second straight for the 32-year-old. And after the way things went in their game against the Chicago Blackhawks last week, there is little reason to believe that the organization feels Stolarz is their best bet to win. While the decision to go with Stolarz may be nothing more than a practical one aimed at giving Bobrovsky some time off, the fact is that the situation in Toronto has gotten too loud to ignore. The Maple Leafs are desperate to get back into the win column. And the bulk of the chatter has placed a fair part of the blame on Sergei Bobrovsky’s shoulders. That’s why it shouldn’t be surprising to see the Leafs going with this plan for now. Of course, the organization will need to make a long-term decision regarding Bobrovsky. If this is just a temporary blip, fans should see the veteran netminder back in the crease sooner rather than later. But if this is a sign of things to come, the Maple Leafs may need to make a permanent call on Bobrovsky before the season really gets away from Toronto. Toronto Knows It Can’t Push Anthony Stolarz Too Hard While Anthony Stolarz is a capable netminder, the Maple Leafs know they can’t push him too hard The Leafs know that, as good as Stolarz can be, fatigue and injury issues arise when he’s asked to shoulder a load for too long. That much was evident last season. That is why Sergei Bobrovsky should find himself back in the crease within the next couple of games. The Maple Leafs may be trying to take some pressure off their veteran netminder while allowing him time to reset mentally. If that is the case, giving Stolarz a short run of starts makes sense. It allows Toronto to keep chasing points while Bobrovsky works through what has been a difficult stretch. However, the organization cannot allow that short-term plan to turn into a permanent game plan. Stolarz has proven capable of handling important minutes, but Toronto’s ideal scenario was always a tandem approach. The Maple Leafs figured that playing Stolarz about once a week was going to be the right load management. That’s why the organization needs to resist the temptation to suddenly dump the bulk of the starts on their backup goalie. Maple Leafs Really Have No Other Choice With Sergei Bobrovsky The reality of the matter is that the Maple Leafs don’t really have much of a choice with Sergei Bobrovsky. Toronto doesn’t really have any other way forward. A trade is not a realistic solution, especially with Bobrovsky’s contract and recent performance creating obvious obstacles. Sending him to the minors is not a practical option either. That leaves the Maple Leafs with one path forward: They have to work through this. If the veteran can bounce back, this conversation likely fades away

sports.title: Wojo: Wolverines, Whittingham fight back. Can they do it again in Columbus?
sports.description: ANN ARBOR — Kyle Whittingham and the Wolverines earned respect and applause, and for what it’s worth, likely a bowl bid. Those all count for something, and they’ll count for even more if they follow up with a victory in Columbus next Saturday. But did they earn more time? It’s the question that will linger after another pulsating, final-play outcome, almost as improbable as all the others. The Wolverines handed No. 4 UCLA its first loss, piling drama on top of drama in an 18-16 triple-overtime victory Saturday, Nov. 21, in Michigan Stadium. The home season ended as it began, with a walk-off score and a spontaneous field-storming by the crowd. Whittingham hasn’t had many signature moments here, and I’m not sure one is enough. It’s enough to suddenly make The Game — downgraded this year to “the game” — a hotter stew of debate and discord. Whittingham’s job security rightly is under scrutiny, especially with a new athletic director, Trev Alberts, on the way . Michigan is 6-5 with seven of its games decided on the final possession. Fighting past the Bruins , who were 10-0 and one of two unbeatens left in the country, was gutty and laudable. Meanwhile, the Buckeyes are 7-4 after losing to Nebraska, and Ryan Day is getting heat, just two years removed from a national title. What once appeared to be a rivalry blowout looks much more intriguing now. The Buckeyes have collapsed since quarterback Julian Sayin went down with an injury. And no matter how many times UM’s offense collapses, its defense keeps rising. Whittingham indeed may have bought time, and not just because UM should be headed to a bowl game. Many of us had him fired before Alberts even showed up, and the outcry is understandable. But it’s also why, in today’s crazy college football, you have to let it play out. More: Wojo: New Michigan AD's mission is clear, but ominous for Kyle Whittingham There’s also a chance his quarterback, Bryce Underwood, bought more time, even as the passing game continues to falter. Underwood, reinstated as the starter , made the biggest throws of the game, including a 3-yarder to little-used senior tight end Jalen Hoffman on the game-winning two-point conversion. Under no circumstances, not even after a scandal and abrupt coaching change, is 6-5 acceptable at UM. That said, there have been no circumstances in program history quite like what we’ve witnessed this season. “The (possible coaching) change is above my pay grade,” Whittingham said. “I just know we're waiting to see what the change actually turns out to be. I can say it's been a pleasure working for (former AD) Warde Manuel during these first 10 months here at Michigan. I actually gave him the game ball. But going forward with this win, I don't know exactly how to compare it to the new guy (Alberts), but it was big for our program.” Like many UM games this year, it appeared to be won and lost multiple times. UCLA tied it 10-10 on a 1-yard jump pass from running back Anthony Woods to tight end Brayden Lof

sports.title: John Mateer Leads Sooners to Impressive SEC Victory
sports.description: Oklahoma Sooners quarterback John Mateer (10) flips into the end zone for a touchdown during a college football game between the Oklahoma Sooners (OU) and the Texas A&M Aggies at Gaylord Family - Oklahoma Memorial Stadium in Norman, Okla., Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. Oklahoma won 28-7. Oklahoma Dominates Texas A&M Behind John Mateer’s Four Touchdown Performance The Oklahoma Sooners delivered one of their strongest performances of the season on Saturday, defeating Texas A&M 28-7 at Gaylord Family Oklahoma Memorial Stadium. Behind a four-touchdown performance from quarterback John Mateer and a dominant defensive effort, Oklahoma secured its third consecutive victory. The Sooners entered the matchup looking to finish their home schedule on a high note. They faced a Texas A&M team starting freshman quarterback Brady Hart, who was making his first collegiate start. After a competitive first half, Oklahoma took control late and pulled away for an important SEC victory. Oklahoma improved to 7-4 overall and 5-3 in conference play, while Texas A&M fell to 4-7 and 1-7 in the SEC. John Mateer Leads the Offensive Breakthrough Mateer was the biggest difference maker for Oklahoma, overcoming two early turnovers to lead the Sooners to a convincing victory. He completed 23 of 34 passes for 269 yards and three touchdowns while adding 66 rushing yards and another score on the ground. Oklahoma initially struggled to find its rhythm, and Texas A&M took a 7-0 lead in the second quarter after Hart connected with Isaiah Horton for a 36 yard touchdown. The Sooners answered before halftime with a 92 yard scoring drive. Mateer completed seven of eight passes on the possession, finishing it with a four yard touchdown throw to Rocky Beers to tie the game at 7-7. The game remained tied through the third quarter before Oklahoma’s offense finally broke through in the fourth. Mateer guided a 96-yard drive that lasted more than eight minutes, finding Tory Blaylock for a five yard touchdown to give the Sooners a 14-7 advantage. Later, following an interception, Mateer connected with Isaiah Sategna for a 25 yard touchdown. He added a seven-yard rushing touchdown in the closing seconds to complete the scoring. Oklahoma Defense Controls the Game While Mateer received plenty of attention, Oklahoma’s defense played an equally important role in the victory. The Sooners limited Texas A&M to just 185 total yards, including 54 rushing yards and 131 passing yards. They also forced eight punts and recorded three sacks. After allowing the Aggies to score on their 96-yard drive in the second quarter, Oklahoma completely shut down the opposing offense. Texas A&M managed only 89 yards after that scoring possession, struggling to sustain drives or create consistent opportunities. Hart finished with eight completions on 20 attempts for 131 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Oklahoma’s defensive pressure made life difficult for the young quarterback throughout the afternoon. Sooners Build Mom

science.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. Following the sad news of Sir Patrick Stewart's passing , there's been no shortage of discussion about his best moments as Captain Jean-Luc Picard . "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command". But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend. With the Borg overrunning the newly launched USS Enterprise-E, Picard — who has long-standing beef with the Collective, following his assimilation in classic "The Next Generation" story " The Best of Both Worlds " — orders his crew to fight the cybernetic nasties hand-to-hand if required, defying their pleas to activate the ship's self-destruct system and retreat. science.title: SpaceX will retire 1st Starship upper stage ever caught by 'chopsticks,' Elon Musk says
science.description: null The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit . He didn't say where Ship would be put on display, but the likeliest locale is Starbase, SpaceX's Starship manufacturing and launch hub. (SpaceX plans to shift most Starship launches to its new Starbase Louisiana site, but construction has yet to begin on that $100 billion complex.) Musk participated virtually in the TomorrowX conversation, which was moderated by two friends of his, the venture capitalists Gavin Baker and Antonio Gracias. (TomorrowX took place in Austin, Texas, but Musk was in China on Wednesday as part of President Trump's delegation for his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.) The world's richest man expounded on Ship 42's historic achievement, explaining that it gets SpaceX much closer to the "holy grail of rocketry" — a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. Before Flight 15, SpaceX had already caught Starship's first-stage booster, known as Super Heavy, on three separate occasions , and it had reflown a booster twice. But the company had never attempted a Ship catch, which is a taller order, given how much faster and farther Starship upper stages fly. So snagging Ship on the first try was a very big deal, according to Musk. "Everyone knew, within SpaceX, at least, how important this milestone was, and that it was really something fundamental and profound — that Starship will be the first-ever fully reusable orbital space system," he told Baker and Gracias on Wednesday. The Ship upper stage of SpaceX's Starship megarocket comes back to its launch tower for a "chopsticks" catch on Nov. 14, 2026, during the vehicle's 15th test flight. science.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today
science.description: null Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio. The duo launched — along with a power and propulsion element called the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) — aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana in October 2018 , beginning a long and looping trip through the inner solar system. Mercury is a difficult planet to reach because it's so close to the sun . Spacecraft approaching the solar system's innermost planet are accelerated to high velocities by the immense gravitational pull of our star and must shed a great deal of kinetic energy to be captured by Mercury's much weaker tug. So the BepiColombo team designed a trajectory that featured one flyby of Earth , two of Venus and six of Mercury over the course of about seven years. That flight time was increased by a year , however, after the mission suffered an issue with its solar panels, which reduced the power available for the MTM's electric thrusters. BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury will take a total of about six months. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Today's orbital insertion is the latest milestone in BepiColombo's Mercury arrival phase, which is expected to take about six months in total. Arrival began on Sept. 3, when the MTM released MPO and Mio. The two orbiters remain connected today; they won't separate until Dec. 9 or thereabouts. Shortly thereafter, Mio will settle into its final orbit, a highly elliptical path that will take it over Mercury's poles. MPO is also destined for a polar orbit, though a much less elliptical one than Mio's; the ESA probe will conduct a series of engine burns before finally getting there on March 10, 2027. BepiColombo won't start doing science work until April 6, 2027. The two probes will gather complementary data from their two different vantage points, shedding a great deal of light on a mysterious world. "The mission will study all aspects of Mercury, from the structure and dynamics of its magnetosphere and how it interacts with the solar wind , to its internal structure with its large iron core, and the origin of the planet’s magnetic field," ESA officials wrote in a BepiColombo mission description . "The data will enable scientists to understand more about the origin and evolution of a planet located close to its parent star, and a better understanding of the overall evolution of our solar system," they added.
